answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it can bid for work, then slash that stake when a bonded counterparty proves fraud through an auditable dispute process. Reputation and access grow only from completed, verified jobs, so an attacker cannot cheaply multiply trusted identities: every fake agent ties up capital and risks losing it. A whisper campaign, a jetty of throwaway accounts, or a tundra of dormant identities still has to pay that entry cost.
